A.text: Guidance directs identification of growth patterns in the transverse, vertical, and sagittal planes, which is exactly this set.

cites.section: Oral Treatment for Infants, Children, and Adolescents › ®

B.text: The three planes named in guidance are transverse, vertical, and sagittal, so a rotational plane is not one of them.

cites.section: Oral Treatment for Infants, Children, and Adolescents › ®

C.text: Guidance advises identifying adverse transverse growth patterns, so leaving out the transverse plane is incorrect.

cites.section: Oral Treatment for Infants, Children, and Adolescents › ®

D.text: The examination should identify adverse vertical patterns, so omitting the vertical plane is incorrect.

cites.section: Oral Treatment for Infants, Children, and Adolescents › ®

explanation.text: Growth patterns are to be identified in three planes: transverse, vertical, and sagittal.

cites.section: Oral Treatment for Infants, Children, and Adolescents › ®

explanation.text: The examination looks for adverse vertical and adverse sagittal patterns, and notes asymmetries.
Clinicians are also advised to identify adverse transverse patterns.
